rule: ruling:sam-2026-10-07 claims 1, 8 and 11: the prototype (Design Release 2.1) wins by default over what the real services do today, and nothing but a DR1 judgement on the same difference or a real constraint the prototype cannot express overrides it; neither exists here, so the prototype's clause and GOV.UK link are adopted, and claim 13 keeps a question only for a truly exceptional difference, which a placeholder href on a link whose design is settled is not.
outcome: The prototype wins: the CPH help's second paragraph reads 'You can find your CPH number on documents from the Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA) or by checking your holding details on GOV.UK.', in English and Welsh, with 'checking your holding details on GOV.UK' as a link. The prototype's href is only a placeholder ('#'), so the link opens the GOV.UK page its text names: the 'Get a county parish holding (CPH) number' guidance (https://www.gov.uk/guidance/get-a-county-parish-holding-cph-number). The destination is a content detail, cheap to change if the design team names another page.
